question: A workshop manufactures two products P and Q. One unit of P requires 2 hours on machine A and 1 hour on machine B, while one unit of Q requires 1 hour on machine A and 2 hours on machine B. Machine A is available for at most 10 hours and machine B for at most 8 hours per day. The profit is Rs 300 on each unit of P and Rs 400 on each unit of Q. Formulate the linear programming problem and determine graphically the daily production plan that maximises the profit, together with the maximum profit.

options.A: Maximise $Z=300x+400y$ subject to $2x+y\leq10$, $x+2y\leq8$, $x\geq0$, $y\geq0$; optimal plan $(4,2)$ with maximum profit Rs $2000$
options.B: Maximise $Z=400x+300y$ subject to $2x+y\leq10$, $x+2y\leq8$, $x\geq0$, $y\geq0$; optimal plan $(4,2)$ with maximum profit Rs $2200$
options.C: Maximise $Z=300x+400y$ subject to $x+2y\leq10$, $2x+y\leq8$, $x\geq0$, $y\geq0$; optimal plan $(2,4)$ with maximum profit Rs $2200$
options.D: Minimise $Z=300x+400y$ subject to $2x+y\leq10$, $x+2y\leq8$, $x\geq0$, $y\geq0$; optimal plan $(0,0)$

(i) Maximise $Z=40x+55y$
(ii) ₹$1825$ for $(25,15)$ and ₹$1900$ for $(20,20)$; $(20,20)$ has the lower cost

(i) Minimise $Z=55x+40y$

question:
A manufacturer produces products $A$ and $B$. Each unit of $A$ requires $2$ units of resource I and $1$ unit of resource II, while each unit of $B$ requires $1$ unit of resource I and $2$ units of resource II. At most $12$ units of each resource are available. The profit per unit is ₹300 for $A$ and ₹400 for $B$. Let $x$ and $y$ be the numbers of units produced.
(i) Write the constraints and the profit function.
(ii) Check whether $(5,4)$ is feasible.
(iii) If the feasible corner points are $(0,0)$, $(6,0)$, $(4,4)$ and $(0,6)$, determine the optimal feasible solution.

options.A:
(i) $2x+y\leq12$, $x+2y\leq12$, $x,y\geq0$; maximise $Z=300x+400y$
(ii) $(5,4)$ is feasible
(iii) Optimal solution $(4,4)$ with profit ₹$2800$
options.B:
(i) $2x+y\leq12$, $x+2y\leq12$, $x,y\geq0$; maximise $Z=300x+400y$
(ii) $(5,4)$ is infeasible
(iii) Optimal solution $(4,4)$ with profit ₹$2800$
options.C:
(i) $x+2y\leq12$, $2x+y\leq12$, $x,y\geq0$; minimise $Z=300x+400y$
(ii) $(5,4)$ is infeasible
(iii) Optimal solution $(0,6)$ with profit ₹$2400$
options.D:
(i) $2x+y\geq12$, $x+2y\geq12$, $x,y\geq0$; maximise $Z=400x+300y$
(ii) $(5,4)$ is feasible
(iii) Optimal solution $(6,0)$ with profit ₹$2400$
